title: Idempotents lift uniquely along a locally nilpotent ideal
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal all of whose elements are nilpotent. Then the reduction map $R\to R/I$ induces a bijection from the idempotents of $R$ to the idempotents of $R/I$: every idempotent $\bar e\in R/I$ is the image of exactly one idempotent $e\in R$.

mathlib_searches.query: idempotents lift uniquely along a surjective ring map whose kernel consists of nilpotent elements
idempotent of quotient ring lifts uniquely when kernel is nil ideal

mathlib_searches.results: existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent {R S} [CommRing R] [Ring S] (f : R →+* S) (h : ∀ x ∈ RingHom.ker f, IsNilpotent x) (e : S) (he : e ∈ f.range) (he' : IsIdempotentElem e) : ∃! e', IsIdempotentElem e' ∧ f e' = e (Mathlib.RingTheory.Idempotents)

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: take f = Ideal.Quotient.mk I, whose kernel is I (Ideal.mk_ker, Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean:133), so the hypothesis is that elements of I are nilpotent; every element of R/I is in f.range (Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective); the conclusion ∃! e' idempotent with f e' = e is the bijection on idempotents (the map sends idempotents to idempotents).
